en: The Sūtra on the Most Victorious Dhāraṇī of the Life-Prolonging Vajra of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Empowered by the Radiance of the Hearts of All Tathāgatas, Spoken by the Buddha.
Translated at Daxingshan Monastery by the Grand Master of State Ceremonial, Peer of the Third Rank, Duke of Susuo.

Presented for examination by the Minister of Rites (Honglu), posthumously titled Minister of Works (Sikong) and conferred the posthumous title "Great Discerning and Vast Wisdom" (Dabianzheng Guangzhi); with a fief of three thousand households. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master from Siṃhala, the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra. Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying on the banks of the Gaṅgā River,
together with a great assembly of bhikṣus, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, devas, and humans.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva was present in the assembly.
Abiding in the Tathāgata’s secret samādhi,
he arose from that samādhi and manifested great supernormal powers.
The Buddhas, through their empowerment, proclaim the Vajra Life-Span Dhāraṇī,
so that all sentient beings may increase their lifespan and avoid untimely or violent deaths,
and furthermore, may they attain a vajra-like life-span that is firm and indestructible.
Having accomplished awakening and reached the stage of non-retrogression,
the World-Honored One then gathered from the worlds of the ten directions as many Buddhas as there are sands in the Ganges by means of the radiance that revolves within his mind.
Filling the entirety of space,
each emitted light like Indra’s net;
with this light touching Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, he was inspired to proclaim the *Vajrāyuṣa-sūtra*.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, having attained the heart-seal of all Buddhas,
immediately abided in the Vajra Life-Span Samaya.
From the pores of his body, he emitted immeasurable rays of light, equal in number to motes of dust, pervading the worlds of the ten directions.
By means of his sovereign power of supernatural faculties,
he then spoke this dhāraṇī:
*tadyathā | tre trelare trelare | vanaḍi | svāhā*.
svasti svasti cakra-vartī-gare prasāmadhu sarva-loka-sarva-sattvānām anāthe jñāthe mahājñāthe trele trele he mā-uḥ.
Kau~ 12. He maṇi caṇḍe 13. He maśike 14. Kāravī 15. Kārati 16.
He kuravī 17. Kurare 18. Kuramati 19. Viśamaṇi maṇi 20. Śūḍivā 21. (Note: The numbers refer to the sequence of the mantras.)
21. A-jo-ri; 22. Mi-jo-ri; 23. Ma-vi-lam-ba; 24. Hu-mu hu-mu; 25. Oṃ vajra-yūṣe svāhā. Having spoken this dhāraṇī, [he said:]...
The great earth, mountains, and rivers all trembled;
the hells were shattered and their palaces shook;
and sentient beings suffering from illness were immediately restored to life.
Within the assembly were immeasurable Vajradhara deities who,
with one voice and in unison, also proclaimed it.
The multitude of great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas all assisted in prolonging life by proclaiming the dhāraṇī, so that they might attain adamantine longevity.
At that time, the heart-seals (*cittamudrā*) and empowerments (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of the Buddhas of the ten directions,
as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, caused Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and the Four Heavenly Kings to further increase their adamantine life-span (*vajrāyus*).
At that moment, the World-Honored One snapped his fingers in praise.
"You are truly able to bring swift and excellent benefit to sentient beings.
If there are good men or good women who fear untimely death, premature demise, or inauspicious events,"
Immediately bathe, put on fresh and clean robes, burn incense, scatter flowers,
and recite my Heart Mantra for Prolonging Life;
your lifespan will then increase.
If there are sentient beings suffering from illness who,
seeking longevity, wish to be free from the pain of disease,
they should immediately establish a site of practice (maṇḍala).
In a clean dwelling or at a monastery,
one should invite twenty-one pure monks.
Recite this sutra forty-nine times each,
and separately maintain this dhāraṇī for one hundred thousand recitations;
you will immediately obtain longevity.
The patient will then see a sublime vision within a dream during the night.
Regarding this method for prolonging life, one must first paint an image of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra in the form of a child with a full moon-like countenance.
Wearing a crown of five buddhas,
his right hand holds a vajra,
and his left hand holds a summoning vajra-bell.
His hair-braids are loosely tied, and he sits upon a thousand-petaled precious lotus flower.
Below him is the White Elephant King, who has three heads;
his trunk is curled around a single-pronged vajra.
Each elephant possesses six tusks.
These elephants stand upon four legs atop a great vajra-wheel,
beneath which are five thousand herds of elephants.
Each bore its own wheel.
From the body of the Bodhisattva, light of a hundred jewels was emitted;

beyond the light were entirely white moon-discs, adorned with all manner of colors, each manifesting the image [of the deity]. With reverent devotion toward the pure place, they established the *maṇḍala*.
Instruct a pure monk to uphold this mantra and to recite or even transcribe this sutra; furthermore,
have him recite the Vajrāyus-dhāraṇī one hundred thousand times.
This is because it increases one's lifespan and eliminates untimely death.
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings and others, sustained by the Buddha’s empowerment, assisted Samantabhadra Bodhisattva in extending life, each making a solemn vow.
In whatever place within Jambudvīpa in the Sahā world this Dharma of the sutra circulates, we,
the four kings, shall immediately provide protection and defense to ensure that no untimely deaths or calamities occur.
If this assembly does not descend to this pure maṇḍala as prescribed in this sūtra,
may I lose this majestic radiance and suffer a diminution of my karmic fruition;
may I fall away from the bodhicitta and fail to attain liberation.
At that time, the Tathāgatas of the ten directions empowered all the Vajradhara Bodhisattvas.
With one voice and in unison, they also spoke this longevity-extending dhāraṇī, saying:
"Oṃ vajrayuṣe hūṃ hūṃ śikhire svāhā. Having spoken thus, they ceased.
When all the Tathāgatas and the Vajradhara Bodhisattvas of the ten directions had withdrawn into the midst of space and were no longer visible,
the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Bhagavān, I too, through the empowerment and protective mindfulness of the Buddha’s spiritual power, shall speak a dhāraṇī for the purpose of excluding untimely death: Oṃ vajrayuṣe."
Śvete śvete śvetale svāhā. Having spoken this dhāraṇī, may all sentient beings obtain long life and be free from untimely death or calamity.
At that time, the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I too shall, by means of the Buddha’s empowering spiritual power, proclaim the Life-Extending Dhāraṇī, which says:"
Oṃ vajrayuṣe maṇḍi maṇḍi maṇḍini śoṣa śomū vaḥ svāhā. Having spoken this dhāraṇī, [he said:]...
"Because they shall obtain a lifespan free from premature death or calamity.
At that time, the Celestial King Virūpākṣa addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, by means of the Buddha’s empowered spiritual authority, I too shall assist in proclaiming the Life-Extending Dhāraṇī, which says:"
Oṃ vajrayuṣe cili cili cile. By reciting this dhāraṇī, all sentient beings shall obtain adamantine longevity and be free from untimely death or calamity.
At that time, the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, by the Buddha’s spiritual power, I too shall proclaim the Life-Extending Dhāraṇī, which says:
Oṃ vajrayuṣe maṃtra vaṃ vaṃ vaṃ svāhā. Having spoken this dhāraṇī, he finished.
"May all sentient beings obtain adamantine life-span and be free from untimely death or calamity.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Four Heavenly Kings, saying:
"If there are sentient beings who fear the perils of death, the suffering of illness, or untimely calamities..."
There is such suffering; yet,
by merely transcribing this sutra, upholding, reading, and reciting it,
or by separately holding this dharani, [one shall be freed from it].
Alternatively, one may paint an image of Samantabhadra for the prolongation of life.
Following this method, on the first, eighth, or fifteenth day of the month,
establish a ritual arena and burn forty-nine lamps.
Place sixteen vessels containing flowers, incense, fruits, and medicinal herbs respectively upon the altar;
then, with palms joined in prostration, chant this dhāraṇī aloud and repent for past transgressions.
They shall not fall into the three evil realms.
Upon casting off this body, they shall obtain adamantine life-span and no longer undergo saṃsāra.
This applies to any bhikṣuṇī or members of the fourfold assembly.
By reciting this sutra without neglect or forgetfulness,
one will be freed from the fear of a short life and untimely death,
as well as from evil dreams at night, malevolent enchantments, curses, hideous rākṣasas, the cries of birds, and all manner of strange portents.
Furthermore, they shall not be harmed by water, fire, weapons, or poisons.
They will be embraced and protected by all Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas,
and they shall also receive the protective mindfulness of all Buddhas.
At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished preaching this sutra,
the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, devas, humans, and the fourfold assembly, along with Vaiśravaṇa, the Heavenly King, and all the great multitude, [were filled with joy].
All were greatly rejoiced, believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
Thus concludes the *Buddha-spoken Sūtra of the Most Victorious Dhāraṇī of the Life-prolonging Vajra of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Empowered by the Radiance of the Heart of All Tathāgatas*.
